limitations: sampling methodology (convenience sample) may have introduced bias
no data on caffeine use, stress levels, and chronotype
actigraphy has low specificity for detecting wakefulness within sleep periods
actigraphy is neither sensitive to low light levels nor calibrated for artificial fluorescent lighting
light exposure measurements for workers in office settings without windows may be an underestimate
wrist actigraphy data may not be fully representative of light levels reaching the retina due to covering
data collection methods do not allow for differentiation between natural daylight and artificial lighting
data collection methods do not allow for analysis of specific wavelengths of light exposure
additional benefits of workplaces with windows, such as the roles of views and other dimensions, were not taken into account
